Use the prescribed grammar across contexts, receptively and productively; Higher includes all Foundation grammar.
Apply Foundation tier French grammar.
Form feminine person nouns by adding -e, changing -eur and -en endings, or changing only the article.
Form plurals with -s or -x, or no change for nouns ending in -s or -x.
Use the infinitive as a noun.
Make articles agree in gender and number, and contract le/la to l' before vowels.
Use definite and indefinite articles, including where French differs from English.
Use partitive articles, and de after negatives and quantity expressions.
Use demonstrative, possessive, interrogative and indefinite adjectives.
Use subject pronouns, including on, and tu versus vous.
Place singular direct and indirect object pronouns before the verb.
Use reflexive pronouns, including plural reciprocal meanings, with contraction before vowels.
Use emphatic moi and toi after prepositions.
Use the relative pronoun qui in subject clauses.
Form negatives with ne...pas, jamais, rien and personne.
Form questions by intonation, est-ce que, or inversion with wh-words.
Know regular -er, -ir and -re verb patterns and the irregular aller, avoir, être, faire, including avoir expressions.
Use the present indicative for simple, ongoing and near-future meaning.
Use the perfect tense, with past participle formation and agreement, and été, eu, fait.
Use aller plus infinitive for the future.
Use the imperative in tu and vous forms.
Use the imperfect in the singular for habitual and ongoing meaning.
Use present forms of boire, connaître, courir, croire, écrire, recevoir, rire, suivre, voir.
Use il y a, il y avait, il y aura, il fait plus adjective, il faut and il est for time.
Use devoir, pouvoir, savoir and vouloir plus infinitive in the present, and je voudrais.
Use reflexive verbs in singular and plural.
